title: Fix the Uninitialized Total
description: The program should sum three numbers and print the result.
expectedBehavior: The program should print 30, the sum of 5, 10, and 15.
actualProblem: total is read on the right-hand side of the assignment before it has ever been given a value. Its initial contents are indeterminate garbage left over in memory, so the result is unpredictable rather than 30.
explanation: Unlike some languages, C does not automatically zero-initialize local variables. A variable must be explicitly given a starting value before it's used in a calculation, or the result is undefined.
